message: No detected input validation: The code reads CSV files and processes dataframes without any schema checks, dtype assertions, or value-range guards; only basic try/except for FileNotFoundError and IndexError are present.
No detected untrusted source handling: The S3 upload/download functions are called without any checksum verification, signature validation, or integrity checks on the retrieved data.
No detected label flipping detection: No code validates label distributions, checks label values against an expected set, or uses any label-noise detection tool before training.

No detected data poisoning defenses: The preparation code only converts units and drops rows containing a specific string; there are no outlier detection, statistical anomaly checks, or suspicious-input filtering mechanisms.

No detected model integrity verification: The code saves a model via pickle but no hash check, signature verification, or integrity validation is performed when loading any serialized model or pretrained weights.

No detected label distribution validation: The train function subsets features and response and splits the data, but performs no class balance check, expected-label-set validation, or anomalous sample detection before training.
No detected backdoor or trigger detection: There is no trigger detection, activation-pattern analysis, or gradient anomaly detection anywhere in the training code.
No detected differential privacy: The code uses a standard scikit-learn RandomForestClassifier with no differential privacy library (Opacus, TensorFlow Privacy, DP-SGD, etc.) applied.
No detected adversarial robustness testing: No adversarial robustness testing libraries or techniques (Foolbox, ART, FGSM, PGD) are imported or used anywhere in the code.

No detected metric tampering protection: Although a train/test split is performed, there is no evidence of hashing/signing evaluation data, a fully isolated held-out set enforced by policy, or multiple independent metrics to guard against metric manipulation.

No detected input sanitization: The inference path reads raw CSV data and passes it directly through clean/featurize/model stages with no input shape, range, or schema validation on incoming requests.
No detected output bounds checks: No code is present that checks model output probabilities, guards against NaN predictions, or validates output values before returning results.
No detected prompt injection defenses: The model is a RandomForestClassifier (not an LLM), so prompt-injection defenses are not applicable and none are implemented.
